newsitem.title: USA: Rain slows Indiana corn and soybean plantings.
newsitem.headline: Rain slows Indiana corn and soybean plantings.

text.p: Indiana's corn and soybean plantings slowed from April's record pace but were still ahead of average, the state's agricultural statistics service said in its weekly update.

"Widespread rains slowed tillage operations during much of the week," the report said. "Both corn and soybean planting progress have slipped back behind record levels for this date, which were achieved in 1988."
Corn was 71 percent seeded as of Sunday, nearly double the five-year average of 36 percent. Soybeans were 31 percent seeded, against 12 percent average.

Winter wheat conditions were rated 62 percent good to excellent, compared with 32 percent at this time last year. Wheat was 89 percent jointed, against 72 percent average. Ten percent was headed, against 12 percent average.
Topsoil moisture was rated nil very short, three percent short, 60 percent adequate and 37 percent surplus.
Pastures were rated two percent very poor, seven percent poor, 34 percent fair, 48 percent good and nine percent excellent.
